# Threadkeep
> Lightweight pure front-end browser extension built on Google Chrome Extensions Manifest V3 for automatically capturing, sanitizing, managing, previewing, and exporting Threads post embed codes together with their structured metadata.

## Core Metadata
- Project Name: Threadkeep (renamed in 2.7.0; formerly "Threads Code Saver" / 「Threads 程式碼儲存器」). The repository was renamed from `threads-embedded-code` to `Threadkeep` (GitHub redirects the old repository URL; the old GitHub Pages URL does not redirect, so use https://scorpio-meow.github.io/Threadkeep/). Console messages use the `[Threadkeep]` prefix.
- Current Version: 2.8.0 (redesign, sound effects, and background music; see the 2.8.0 entry in CHANGELOG.md)
- Specification: Google Chrome Extensions Manifest V3
- Tech Stack: Pure Native JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, CSS3 Custom Properties with `light-dark()`, the Popover API, and the Web Audio API (Zero external dependencies, zero compilation/build step). `manifest.json` sets `minimum_chrome_version` to 123 because of `light-dark()`.
- Data Persistence: Browser local storage (chrome.storage.local with the `unlimitedStorage` permission, so the default 10MB quota does not apply; privacy-first). Saved data never leaves the browser; network access is limited to Threads domains (live preview and background updates) plus the Google Fonts stylesheet imported by ui.css. Sound effects and background music ship inside the extension (`sounds/`).
- Accessibility: In-page modals only (no native confirm/alert/prompt), focus trapping, live regions, 4.5:1 contrast, undersized button hit targets enlarged to at least 24x24px (checkboxes are 16x16px, a known limitation), font sizes limited to 12/14/16/20px, prefers-reduced-motion support (also stops the ambient light, cursor spotlight, and card entrance animations), system or manually chosen light/dark themes, forced-colors (Windows High Contrast) styles, pausable toasts, optional sound that only supplements visible and announced feedback; axe-core 4.10.2 reports no violations on 10 popup/dashboard states in light and dark
- License: MIT ([LICENSE](./LICENSE))
- Source Repository: https://github.com/Scorpio-meow/Threadkeep
- Companion Showcase Site: Threadfolio, live example https://scorpio-meow.github.io/Threadfolio-Example/, source https://github.com/Scorpio-meow/Threadfolio-Example (consumes exported featured post data as its primary dataset)

## Core Files
- [manifest.json](./manifest.json): Extension configuration manifest declaring Manifest V3 specs, permissions (storage, unlimitedStorage, tabs, scripting), host matches for threads.com and threads.net, `all_frames: true` content script injection (`article-store.js`, `sound.js`, then `content.js`), strict CSP headers, `minimum_chrome_version: "123"`, and `web_accessible_resources` that expose only `sounds/save.ogg` and `sounds/error.ogg` to the four Threads hosts.
- [theme.js](./theme.js): Theme preference script loaded in the `<head>` of the popup and dashboard; applies the cached `data-theme` immediately, syncs with `chrome.storage.local`, and wires the "外觀" select inside the dashboard's 「設定」 popover menu.
- [article-store.js](./article-store.js): Shared storage layer loaded by the content script, the popup, and the dashboard. It derives each post's storage key, migrates the legacy `savedArticles` array, reads, writes, and removes individual records, merges batch-update fields into stored records, and applies per-key `chrome.storage.onChanged` events to an in-memory list. It also holds the preference storage keys (`THEME_PREFERENCE_KEY` = `themePreference`, used by theme.js and content.js; `SOUND_EFFECTS_KEY` = `soundEffects` and `BACKGROUND_MUSIC_KEY` = `backgroundMusic`, used by sound.js) and the shared embeddable-check helpers (`getThreadsEmbedPath`, `checkEmbeddable`, `applyEmbeddableResult`, `pickEmbeddableFields`).
- [content.js](./content.js): Primary Content Script. On Threads pages it listens for clicks on the "Get embed code" item through a single delegated capture-phase listener, checks for the official embed dialog at most once per animation frame after DOM mutations (no page-wide button scans or periodic polling), intercepts the dialog, and after a click waits up to 8 seconds (`EMBED_DIALOG_TIMEOUT_MS`, checking every 250ms) for the embed code before reporting a missing dialog or empty dialog; if Threads shows its own error message ("發生錯誤…技術錯誤" / "Something went wrong", outside post containers) during that wait, it stops and reports immediately that Threads failed and the post was not saved. It also scores embed candidates, extracts top-level text containers, filters image-only descriptions, and strips UI/timestamp noise. Every save or error notification also calls `playSound('save')` or `playSound('error')` from sound.js. Inside `/embed` iframes it switches to `handleEmbedFrameResize()` and reports the measured `.Embed` height to the parent window.
- [styles.css](./styles.css): Injected notification styles for Threads web pages (ink #1a1814 with a champagne hairline, #22201c in dark mode, red for errors), including live-region toast styling and prefers-reduced-motion fallbacks.
- [ui.css](./ui.css): Shared design system loaded by the popup and the dashboard before their own stylesheets: `light-dark()` color tokens, fonts and font sizes, radii, motion curves, and shared components (`.btn` variants, `.field`, `.select`, `.search`, `.check`, `.switch` with `role="switch"`, `.menu` popovers, `.modal-*`, `.choice-*`, `.toast*`, `.tag-chip`, `.badge`, `.empty-state`, `.copy-btn` feedback), the drifting ambient light (`body::before`), the cursor spotlight (`body::after`), the per-card spotlight (`.article-card::before`), and reduced-motion / forced-colors fallbacks.
- [ui.js](./ui.js): Shared behavior. `setupMenus()` positions each `.menu[popover]` under its `popovertarget` trigger (flipping above when there is no room, aligned to the trigger's end unless `data-align="start"`), closes it after a `button.menu-item` click, and closes open menus on resize. `setupAmbientLight()` tracks the pointer (ignoring touch) with at most one `requestAnimationFrame` per frame, writing `--pointer-x`/`--pointer-y` on `<html>` (plus `data-pointer="active"`, removed on mouseleave) and `--spot-x`/`--spot-y` on the hovered `.article-card`.
- [sound.js](./sound.js): Sound layer shared by the popup, the dashboard, and the content script. It reads `soundEffects` (anything but `false` means on) and `backgroundMusic` (only `true` means on) and follows `chrome.storage.onChanged`. `playSound(name)` fetches `chrome.runtime.getURL('sounds/<name>.ogg')` once, decodes it with `AudioContext.decodeAudioData`, and plays it at gain 0.6, silently skipping when the audio context cannot start. `setupBackgroundMusic()` (dashboard only) loops `sounds/background-music.ogg` with an `AudioBufferSourceNode` (`loop = true`, gain 0.3, 1.8s fade-in, 0.4s fade-out), stops when the tab is hidden and restarts from the beginning when visible, and waits for the first pointerdown/keydown when autoplay is blocked. `setupSoundSwitches()` binds the two switches and plays the save sound when effects are turned on.
- [sounds/](./sounds/): Ogg Opus 48kHz assets rendered with the local XSXB-Band studio from CC0 sampled instruments (no generative model): `save`, `copy`, `delete`, `undo`, `complete`, `error` (mono, about 56 kbps, 0.32-1.12s, harp and piano in D major) and `background-music` (stereo, about 96 kbps, an exactly 120-second seamless loop of neo-classical piano, violins, cellos, and harp at 64 BPM).
- [popup.html](./popup.html): 480x600px browser toolbar popup markup: a header with 「開啟控制面板」 and a 「更多」 popover menu (three exports with hints, 「匯入…」, 「清除全部」), search, filter and sort selects, a list bar (select-all, count, 「已選取 N 篇」, 「取消選取」), the single-column card list, and the confirm, import-source, import-paste, and import-mode modals.
- [popup.css](./popup.css): Popup layout only (header, toolbar, list bar, single-column cards with hairline borders); shared components come from ui.css.
- [popup.js](./popup.js): Toolbar popup controller supporting debounced keyword search (180ms), 6 sorting rules, 6 filter categories, single-item maintenance, undoable deletion, in-page modals, file/paste import, selection-aware export, and sound effects.
- [dashboard.html](./dashboard.html): Full-page dashboard (控制面板) markup: a glass top bar (brand, search, 「前往 Threads」, the 「設定」 popover with the theme select and the sound/music switches), a sidebar `nav` (welcome card, 2x2 view grid, tag cloud, author cloud, 資料 buttons with the export popover and update progress), the masonry card list with its header and batch bar, the preview drawer (loading and error states), and confirmation/import modals.
- [dashboard.css](./dashboard.css): Dashboard layout: top bar, sidebar view grid and clouds, the 4px-row masonry grid, card states, the preview drawer and scrim, responsive rules (single column under 760px), and forced-colors overrides.
- [dashboard.js](./dashboard.js): Dashboard core controller managing filter navigation, masonry sizing, the preview drawer, the sequential asynchronous update queue (with pause/resume/cancel signals), tag/author clouds, batch operations, undo snapshots, in-page confirmation dialogs, the greeting card, and sound/music wiring.
- [icons/](./icons/): Extension icons at 16, 32, 48, and 128 px (`icon-16.png`, `icon-32.png`, `icon-48.png`, `icon-128.png`).
- [images/](./images/): `mascot-320.webp`, the scorpion-cat mascot shown in the popup and dashboard empty states (no saved posts, or no posts matching the current filter), the dashboard welcome card, and the preview drawer while it loads. It is a copy of `docs/assets/img/mascot-320.webp`.
- [README.md](./README.md): Comprehensive Traditional Chinese technical documentation with Mermaid diagrams, schemas, and developer guide.
- [CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md): Version history in Traditional Chinese, following Keep a Changelog. The README's changelog section only links here.
- [llms.txt](./llms.txt): Structured technical specifications for AI agents and LLM/RAG indexing pipelines.
- [docs/](./docs/): GitHub Pages introduction site, not shipped with the extension. Its interactive cleaning demo (`docs/assets/js/cleaner-worker.js`) fetches `content.js` from the `main` branch inside a Web Worker and calls `cleanExtractedPostContent` and `isLikelyThreadsFallbackDescription` directly, so renaming or removing either function breaks the demo. The version shown on the page is read from the `main` branch's `manifest.json` the same way. Screenshots live in `docs/assets/img/`, each with a `-dark` variant swapped in by `syncThemedImages()` in `site.js`. `docs/assets/video/` holds the muted tag-filter demo loop (`tag-filter.mp4` and `tag-filter-dark.mp4`, with webp posters) for the 「標籤與作者排行」 tab: it autoplays only when visible and when reduced motion is not requested, shows only the poster under reduced motion or without JavaScript, and has a play/pause button.

## Data Models & Schema
Each post is one SavedArticle object stored under its own key in `chrome.storage.local`. The key is `post:` plus the post code from the permalink (for example `post:DezKX7tE_q9`); imported records without a recognizable link use `post:id:<id>`. The same post under threads.com and threads.net maps to the same key, so saving it again overwrites the record, except that the previous `embeddable` and `embeddableCheckedAt` are kept until the background re-check that follows the save. Views load all `post:` keys and order them by `savedAt`, newest first.

Versions up to 2.2.1 stored every post in one array under the `savedArticles` key. The first time the popup or dashboard opens, or the content script saves a post, `migrateLegacyArticles` splits that array into per-post records: it writes only keys that do not exist yet (newer records are never overwritten), keeps the earliest array entry (the newest save) when the same post appears twice, reads the keys back to confirm they were all written, and only then removes `savedArticles`. Older versions cannot read migrated data.

### SavedArticle Interface
```typescript
interface SavedArticle {
  /** Unique primary identifier (new saves: embed_[timestamp]_[random]; imports: imported_[timestamp]_[random], or the id carried by the source file) */
  id: string;

  /** Canonical Threads post URL, used as unique key for deduplication and updates */
  postLink: string;

  /** Official Threads native <blockquote> embed HTML code */
  embedCode: string;

  /** Publication timestamp in ISO 8601 standard format */
  timestamp: string;

  /** Formatted publication title string (e.g., "May 29, 2026, 10:00 AM") */
  timestampTitle: string;

  /** Local storage timestamp in ISO 8601 format */
  savedAt: string;

  /** Sanitized plaintext content preserving natural paragraph line breaks */
  content: string;

  /** Author handle from the post header's author link text (normally without @, e.g., "username"), falling back to the username in postLink, then to "未知作者" */
  author: string;

  /** Tags from official hashtag links and inline #hashtags */
  tags: string[];

  /** Post operational status */
  status: 'active' | 'expired';

  /** Timestamp when the post was marked as expired (ISO 8601) */
  expiredAt?: string;

  /** Specific reason for expiration */
  expiredReason?: 'redirected' | 'post-not-found' | 'fallback-summary' | 'unknown';

  /** Timestamp of the last status check attempt (ISO 8601) */
  expiredCheckedAt?: string;

  /** Timestamp when publication timestamp was last updated (ISO 8601) */
  timestampUpdatedAt?: string;

  /** Whether Threads serves an embed card to a cookieless request: false when /embed answers HTTP 500, true when it answers 200 with a .Embed container; absent until a check is conclusive, and later inconclusive checks keep the previous value */
  embeddable?: boolean;

  /** When the last conclusive embeddable check ran (ISO 8601) */
  embeddableCheckedAt?: string;

  /** Source format indicator, set only by popup .js imports (dashboard imports and .json imports leave it unset) */
  importedFrom?: 'full-data-file' | 'js-embed-file';
}
```

### Removed in 2.2.0
- The `authorUrl` field was removed. Nothing read it (UI, search, filters, statistics, and all three exports ignored it), and it can be derived from `author` or `postLink`. Newly saved and imported records no longer include it; records saved by older versions may still hold a stale value, which nothing reads.

### Removed in 2.1.0 (Breaking Change)
- The `codeBlocks: CodeBlock[]` and `codeCount: number` fields, the `CodeBlock` interface, and all related UI (code cards, code search, code copy buttons, and the code import field) were removed.
- The extraction logic had been unreachable since the embed-dialog capture flow replaced the legacy save flow, so newly saved records always contained an empty array.
- Importing an older backup no longer preserves these fields, and code text is no longer part of the search index. Since 2.2.1, search matches `content`, `author`, `tags`, and the path part of `postLink` (without the domain), which is also what both search inputs advertise; `embedCode` was searched before that, but its fixed official boilerplate made terms such as "threads" match every post.
- Follow-up cleanup: `refreshEmbedCode` and its private `buildThreadsEmbedCode` copy were deleted from popup.js because their button had already been removed from the markup, and the `lastUpdated` field they wrote was dropped from the schema. Exports and imports never carried it; only records saved by older versions may still hold a stale value, which nothing reads.

## Key Concepts & Algorithms

### 1. Top-Level Text Container Layout Extraction
- Targets primary content nodes: `span[class*="xo1l8bm"][dir="auto"]`, `span[class*="xi7mnp6"][dir="auto"]`, and `div[class*="x1iorvi4"][dir="auto"]`.
- Strictly ignores `time` tags, permalink tags (`a[href*="/post/"]`, `a[href*="/t/"]`), author header links (`a[href*="/@"]`), topic and trending-topic chips (`a[href*="/search"]`), and Meta AI promotional text.
- Drops containers that hold real media (`video`, `picture`, `canvas`, or an `img` without `aria-hidden="true"`); inline GIF stickers and emoji images inside the post text are marked `aria-hidden="true"` and do not cause the text to be discarded.
- On single post pages, the `threads_post_page_0` pagelet is only used as the search root when it contains text; Threads now renders it as an empty placeholder and puts the target post in a later pagelet, so the post is located through its permalink instead.
- Applies `isLikelyImageOnlyDescription` heuristic to filter out media captions.
- Deduplicates containers hierarchically and invokes `innerText.trim()`, preserving paragraph breaks and `<br>` elements without whitespace collapse.

### 2. Embed Dialog Weighted Scoring Algorithm
- Scans all readonly input fields within the embed modal and scores candidates:
  - Base string length score
  - Contains `data-text-post-permalink`: +1000 points
  - Contains `<blockquote`: +500 points
  - Contains `threads.com`: +100 points
- Selects the highest-scoring candidate to ensure 100% complete blockquote retrieval.

### 3. Tag Extraction & Normalization
- `extractTags` merges two sources: official hashtag anchors (`a[href*="serp_type=tags"]`, `a[href*="tag_id="]`, reading the `q` query parameter first and falling back to link text), and inline hashtags: a `#` or full-width `＃` followed by letters, combining marks, digits or underscores in any script with at least one letter (`/(?<![\p{Script=Latin}\p{Script=Greek}\p{Script=Cyrillic}\p{N}\p{M}_&\/])[#＃](?![\uFE0F\u20E3])([\p{L}\p{M}\p{N}_]*\p{L}[\p{L}\p{M}\p{N}_]*)/gu`), scanned after removing `http(s)://` and `www.` URLs. A `#` directly after a Latin, Greek or Cyrillic letter, a digit, `_`, `&` or `/` does not start a tag, so URL fragments, `C#12` and `&#39;` are skipped, as are all-digit tags such as `#2024` and the keycap emoji; a `#` right after a CJK character (for example 去吃#台南美食) still counts. Words without a `#` never become tags.
- Removed in 2.7.0: the 12-entry technology keyword map (JavaScript, Python, Java, C++, C#, HTML, CSS, SQL, TypeScript, React, Vue, Angular) that added tags from plain words in the content. Its patterns were unreliable (`\bC#\b` only matched forms like "C#12"; C++ had no word boundary and matched inside "ABC++"). Posts saved earlier keep those tags until "更新貼文資料" re-extracts them.
- All tags are normalized with `String.prototype.normalize('NFC')` and deduplicated case-insensitively, keeping the first spelling (so an official `JavaScript` hashtag link and an inline `#javascript` do not both appear).
- The injected `extractPostInfoFromPage` used by the background update queue keeps no copy of the extraction logic: it calls `findPostElementFromPostLink`, `extractPostContent`, and `extractTags` from the `content.js` instance already running on the Threads page (same isolated world), waiting until that content script is available. Updated content and tags therefore match what saving produces. It still handles not-found detection, datetime lookup (`time[datetime]`, `article:published_time`, JSON-LD), and marks a post `fallback-summary` expired when the post has no datetime or content and `og:description` is a platform placeholder.

### 4. 44-Rule Noise & Timestamp Filtering Pipeline
- `cleanExtractedPostContent` normalizes whitespace, strips carousel counters (e.g., 1/5), translation buttons, and "view original" labels, then collapses redundant blank lines.
- `isLikelyThreadsFallbackDescription` evaluates every line against 44 regular expressions covering relative timestamps (e.g., "2d", "1h", "just now", "yesterday"), follower metrics, thread counts, view counts, post header labels ("Pinned", "Author", lone "·" separators), and navigation items across Traditional Chinese and English UI locales. Matching lines are dropped entirely.

### 5. Live Preview Protocol & Dynamic Height Adaptation
- The preview is a drawer (`#inspector`, `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`) that slides in from the right over a scrim at every viewport width; it is opened by the author button in a card header or a click on empty card space (ignored while text is selected), and `activateModal` traps focus in it with initial focus on the close button.
- Dual-tab interface supporting Official Embed preview and Raw Source/Metadata inspection (the raw tab also shows the full post text).
- The drawer is at most 560px wide (`min(560px, 100vw)`) and the embed iframe scales with it up to 560px. The 658px fixed width and the multi-device width switcher are gone.
- Height adaptation: because the official `/embed` page only posts an untyped numeric string to its parent (indistinguishable from other messages), `content.js` is injected into the preview iframe (`all_frames: true`) and measures the `.Embed` container with a ResizeObserver on that container and on the body's first child (a childList-only MutationObserver re-attaches it when the container is replaced). Measurements are coalesced to at most one per animation frame, and `{ type: 'THREADS_EMBED_RESIZE', height }` is posted to the parent window only when the height changes. When Threads will not embed a post (deleted, private, or limited to logged-in viewers, for example as sensitive content), `/embed` answers HTTP 500 with a Meta error page that still fires the iframe `load` event (the preview loads from `www.threads.com`, where the Threads session lives, so posts limited to logged-in viewers do render in the preview when the browser is logged in to Threads, while on a third-party site only visitors who are logged in to Threads and allow third-party cookies can see them); on an `/embed` page with no `.Embed` container `content.js` posts `{ type: 'THREADS_EMBED_ERROR' }` instead, and the dashboard (after checking that `event.source` is the preview iframe) shows its own error state, hides the error page, and keeps the later `load` event from flipping the state back to ready. `content.js` matches every threads.com frame, including Threads embeds on other websites, but it only posts when its direct parent is one of this extension's pages (the host of `location.ancestorOrigins[0]` must equal `chrome.runtime.id`), and it targets that origin instead of `'*'`, so other sites never receive `THREADS_EMBED_RESIZE` or `THREADS_EMBED_ERROR`. The `Permissions-Policy` console warnings about `attribution-reporting` and `shared-storage` come from Meta's response headers and are unrelated to embed failures.
- The dashboard validates `event.origin` against `threads.net`, `threads.com`, and `instagram.com`, and takes the height from `THREADS_EMBED_RESIZE.height`, then `details.height` (the official `MEASURE` shape; a string `details` is JSON-parsed), then a bare `height` or `scrollHeight`, applying only values between 100px and 5000px. `THREADS_EMBED_ERROR` is honored only when `event.source` is the current preview iframe.
- Explicit load states: a floating mascot loader, a 10-second timeout state, and a load-failure state, the latter two offering a retry button. Posts without a usable link show a non-retryable message pointing to the Raw Source tab.
- Keyboard navigation: ESC, the scrim, or the close button close the drawer and return focus to the previewed card's author button; Left Arrow / Right Arrow (ignored on tab buttons) move to the previous/next post, scroll the matching card into view behind the scrim, and mark it with a 2px champagne outline (`.is-current`).

### 6. Background Sequential Update Queue
- Queue scope: the checked posts within the current filtered list when any are checked (checked posts later filtered out are skipped), otherwise the filtered and sorted list. The sidebar 資料 「更新資料」 button and the batch bar's 「更新資料」 both call `updateAllTimestamps` and behave the same. Progress appears under the sidebar buttons and as 「更新中 X/Y」 in the top bar; the pause button toggles 「暫停」/「繼續」 (the progress bar turns amber while paused) and 「停止」 cancels.
- Executes updates sequentially inside a single reusable hidden tab (`chrome.tabs.update`) to eliminate rate limiting or high CPU usage. The tab is closed on extraction failure and in the `finally` block once the queue ends.
- Safety cap: `fetchPostInfoWithReusableTab` waits at most 60 seconds (`POST_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS`) for navigation plus extraction. A timeout returns `null`, which counts as a failure and closes the worker tab; it never marks the post as expired.
- Embeddable check: after loading each post, the queue runs `checkEmbeddable` (from `article-store.js`) inside the threads.com worker tab via `chrome.scripting.executeScript`, as a same-origin `fetch` of the post's `/embed` with `credentials: 'omit'`. HTTP 500 sets `embeddable: false`, a 200 response containing `class="Embed"` sets `true`, and anything else (timeout, rate limit, other responses) leaves the previous value alone; conclusive results also set `embeddableCheckedAt`. The check must run in a threads.com tab: a cross-site fetch from an extension page only receives Threads' generic app shell. `content.js` runs the same check once in the background after saving a post. Both fields are in `ARTICLE_UPDATE_FIELDS`, the featured and full exports include them when present (`pickEmbeddableFields`), and imports keep them. The injected extractor runs its check from a `MutationObserver`, at most once per 80ms (`POST_INFO_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS`), so it reacts as soon as the page renders and is not slowed by background-tab timer throttling.
- Supports pause, resume, and cancellation signals. Results are persisted every 20 posts (`UPDATE_PERSIST_BATCH_SIZE`), when pausing, and when the queue ends. Each write (`mergeArticleUpdates`) reads only the keys of the pending posts, copies `ARTICLE_UPDATE_FIELDS` (`timestamp`, `timestampTitle`, `content`, `tags`, expired status fields, `timestampUpdatedAt`, `embeddable`, `embeddableCheckedAt`) from the in-memory records onto the stored records, deleting any of these fields the in-memory record lacks, and skips keys that no longer exist, so posts deleted during the queue are not resurrected and posts saved on Threads meanwhile are untouched. Closing the page mid-run loses at most the last 19 unsaved updates.
- During the run only the updated card and the view counts are re-rendered; filters, clouds, and the full list refresh once the queue ends. A completed, uncancelled run without write errors plays the `complete` sound.
- Automatically marks posts as expired on redirect, post-not-found (404/deleted), or platform fallback summary, and restores them to active once accessible again.

### 7. 6 Filter Dimensions & 6 Sorting Rules
- Filter Categories:
  - `all`: All stored posts
  - `author`: Filter by specific author handle
  - `tag`: Filter by specific hashtag/topic
  - `noContent`: Posts without a text body (image-only or empty descriptions)
  - `noTimestamp`: Posts lacking a timestamp or requiring synchronization
  - `expired`: Deleted, privatized, or redirected posts
- Dashboard: `all`, `expired`, `noContent`, and `noTimestamp` are a 2x2 view grid at the top of the sidebar, each button showing its count (the expired count turns red when non-zero); `author` and `tag` come from the sidebar clouds and the tag chips on cards (`toggleFilter` clears the filter when the active item is clicked again). The list header title shows the current filter (`data-title` of the view button, `#tag`, or the author) and the result count.
- Popup: a filter select plus a second value select for `author` and `tag`.
- Sorting Rules (dashboard label / popup label):
  - `savedAt-desc` / `savedAt-asc`: 儲存時間（新到舊／舊到新） / 最新儲存、最早儲存
  - `timestamp-desc` / `timestamp-asc`: 發文時間（新到舊／舊到新） / 最新發文、最早發文
  - `author-asc` / `author-desc`: 作者（A-Z／Z-A） / 作者 A–Z、作者 Z–A
- Dashboard cards show the saved time when sorting by `savedAt`, otherwise the post time, with the full date in `title`.
- The legacy "code count" sorting option was removed in 2.1.0.

### 8. Accessibility & Recoverable Operations
- Native `confirm()`, `alert()`, and `prompt()` are never used. Every dialog is an in-page modal with `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, a labelled title (the confirm and import-mode dialogs also have `aria-describedby`), initial focus, Tab focus trapping, ESC dismissal, and focus restoration to the triggering control. This matters most in the MV3 popup, where a native dialog is dismissed together with the popup on blur and returns its default value.
- Destructive actions are recoverable: single delete, batch delete, and clear-all show an undo toast (8 seconds by default, `UNDO_TOAST_DURATION_MS`). The countdown pauses while the pointer is over the toast or keyboard focus is on its undo button. Only one undo toast exists at a time, so an older snapshot can never roll back newer changes.
- Overwrite imports require a second confirmation modal; dismissing it or pressing ESC always cancels.
- The dashboard batch bar (更新資料, 複製內嵌碼, 刪除, 取消選取) replaces the list header only while posts are selected; select-all is disabled when there are no results. Disabled controls use the `disabled` attribute rather than `pointer-events: none`, so keyboard activation is blocked as well. 「取消選取」 moves focus to select-all in both views.
- Toast containers and injected Threads notifications are live regions. Popup and dashboard toasts stay `role="status"` / `aria-live="polite"` even for errors (errors only add the `toast-error` class); only injected Threads notifications escalate to `role="alert"` / `assertive` for errors. Regular messages stay at least 4 seconds and errors at least 6 seconds; longer messages get about 120ms per character (`TOAST_DURATION_MS`, `TOAST_ERROR_DURATION_MS`, `TOAST_MS_PER_CHAR`, and the `NOTIFICATION_*` equivalents in content.js). Hovering a toast pauses its countdown. Toast and notification text streams in per character (each grapheme animates from `blur(6px)` and transparent to clear over 90ms with `cubic-bezier(.215,.61,.355,1)`, staggered 30ms); the full sentence sits in a visually hidden span and the animated copy is `aria-hidden`, and reduced motion shows it at once. Copying an embed code shows an in-place "已複製" state on the button (`data-feedback="copied"`, `COPY_FEEDBACK_MS` = 2500) that fades back, and announces the result through `#liveStatus` instead of a toast.
- View grid buttons, tag cloud chips, and author cloud items are `button` elements with `aria-pressed` reflecting the active filter; the 「全部 N 個…」 toggle uses `aria-expanded`. Each cloud is a `role="group"` labelled by its heading, and re-rendering a cloud refocuses the item that had focus (matched by `data-filter-key`). Cloud items get `data-weight` strong (>= 60% of the top count), medium (>= 30%), or light, which only changes font weight. Popover menus (popup 「更多」, dashboard 「設定」 and 「匯出」) live inside the header or sidebar landmarks and are opened with `popovertarget`.
- Card lists are `role="list"` (set only while cards exist) labelled by `#articleListHeading` (the visible current-filter title in the dashboard, a visually hidden 「貼文列表」 in the popup); each card is a `listitem` whose author is an `h3` (in the dashboard the `h3` holds the preview button). The card checkbox and action buttons have `aria-label`s that include the author and post time (`getArticleLabel`, e.g. "刪除：user174 於 18 小時前發布的貼文"). Relative times ("18 小時前") carry the full date and time in a visually hidden span and in `title`. The "show more" button lives in `#loadMoreContainer` below the list, not inside it.
- A visually hidden `#liveStatus` region (`role="status"`, `aria-atomic="true"`) announces result counts after user-triggered search and filter changes (`applyFilters({ announceResults: true })`) and the selection count after checkbox, select-all, or clear-selection changes.
- Re-rendering keeps keyboard focus: `renderArticles` and `refreshRenderedCard` record the focused card and control (`captureCardFocus`) and restore it (`restoreCardFocus`). If the card is gone, focus moves to the card now at the same position, or to the list heading when the list is empty. Undo moves focus to the restored post when focus was on the undo button.
- Controls that can appear inside dialogs or the drawer (`.btn`, `.choice-option`, `.preview-tab`, `.modal-close-btn`) transition only appearance properties, never `all`. The overlay toggles `visibility`, and a descendant that also transitions `visibility` stays hidden for the first frame, which makes the dialog's initial `focus()` call fail.
- Preview tab panels and the raw embed-code block are focusable (`tabindex="0"`) so the scrollable preview can be scrolled from the keyboard; the metadata table uses row headers.
- Search inputs use a 180ms debounce (`SEARCH_DEBOUNCE_MS`); clouds display the top 15 entries (`CLOUD_VISIBLE_LIMIT`, plus the active entry if it ranks lower) with a 「全部 N 個…」 / 「收合」 toggle (`expandedNavGroups`). Tags are grouped case-insensitively by `getTagGroups` (article-store.js): each post counts once per group, and the group is labeled with its most common spelling; the tag cloud, the tag filter options, and the unique-tag statistic all use these groups, and filter selection matches case-insensitively.
- Console output is kept short: saving logs one `console.info` line (`已儲存` / `已更新` plus the storage key); warnings and errors are logged only for real failures.
- Lists render in batches: 60 cards at a time in the dashboard and 30 in the popup (`RENDER_BATCH_SIZE`). A "show more" button below the list loads the next batch when clicked or when an IntersectionObserver sees it near the viewport; clicking it moves focus to the first new card. Card actions are handled by delegated listeners on the list container, and select-all and clear-selection update rendered cards in place. Dashboard masonry: `#articlesContainer` is a CSS grid with `grid-auto-rows: 4px` and `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(min(280px, 100%), 1fr))` columns; a `ResizeObserver` (`masonryObserver`) sets each card's `grid-row-end: span N` from its border-box height plus the column gap, so DOM and Tab order stay in sort order. Cards are not `content-visibility: auto` (their heights must be real). On a non-`keepRendered` render the container gets `is-entering` and cards fade in with a 32ms stagger (`--i`, capped at 12); the popup animates only its first render.
- Search matches `content`, `author`, `tags`, and the path part of `postLink` (`/@author/post/CODE`, without the domain), so a handle or post code finds the post. Each post's lowercased search text is cached in a WeakMap and invalidated when the update queue changes that post. Sorting precomputes one key per post and compares author names with a shared `Intl.Collator('zh-TW')`.
- Both the popup and the dashboard listen to `chrome.storage.onChanged`. Events carry only the changed `post:` keys; `applyStoredArticleChanges` removes deleted records, adds or replaces changed ones, and ignores changes whose value already matches the in-memory record (such as echoes of the page's own writes).
- Saving on Threads writes a single key (about 3 KB) instead of rewriting the whole collection; deleting removes the matching keys. Opening the popup or dashboard still reads every post.
- Text contrast is at least 4.5:1 in light and dark, undersized button hit targets are enlarged to at least 24x24px (checkboxes are an exception: every `.check` is 16x16px; the popup select-all label is 32px tall), font sizes are 12/14/16/20px only, and every stylesheet honors `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
- Theme: the 「外觀」 select in the dashboard's 「設定」 popover offers system, light, or dark. The choice is stored as `themePreference` in `chrome.storage.local` (absent means follow the system) and mirrored to `localStorage` so `theme.js`, loaded in each page's `<head>`, can set `data-theme` on `<html>` before first paint. The popup and the content script's Threads notifications (via a `data-theme` attribute on the notification) follow the same setting and react to `chrome.storage.onChanged`. Colors are defined once on `:root` in ui.css with `light-dark()`; `:root` declares `color-scheme: light dark`, and `data-theme="light"` / `"dark"` force `color-scheme`. Palette (light / dark): paper #f6f3ec / #12110f, sheet #fffdf8 / #1a1916, raised #ffffff / #22201c, ink #1a1814 / #f2ede3 (primary buttons, checkboxes, switches, pressed view and author items), accent champagne #83632a / #d9bc7a (selected and current cards, focus outline, tab underline, progress bar, highlighted numbers), tag chips #f1e9d6 on #6b5020 / #2b261c on #e3c98f, danger #b42318 / #f97066; all text pairs are at least 4.5:1. Focus is a 2px solid `--focus` outline offset 2px on buttons and links and 0 on fields (at least 5:1 against the background). Lines are 0.5px hairlines; radii are 6px for controls and 10px for cards and floating layers. Fonts: Geist and Noto Sans TC for UI text, Geist Mono for code, Playfair Display and Noto Serif TC (`--font-display`, lining numerals) for the brand, list title, drawer title, greeting, and view counts. Font weights drop by 40 in dark mode (`--fw-regular` 400 → 360 and so on). Motion keeps the two `linear()` springs (`--spring-pop` for checkbox ticks and copy checks, `--spring-snap` for dialogs and the drawer); the dashboard card body still collapses with a five-line peek row plus a `0fr` → `1fr` grid row. A `@media (forced-colors: active)` block restores native checkboxes and switches, outlines selected/current cards and pressed view or cloud items with `Highlight`, colors the active preview tab and the progress bar with `Highlight`, borders menus, dialogs, and toasts with `CanvasText`, and uses `GrayText` for disabled buttons.

### 9. Sound Effects & Background Music
- Sound effects (harp and piano, D major, `sounds/*.ogg`): `save` (harp D-F#-A-D arpeggio, 0.74s) when a post is saved or updated on Threads; `copy` (piano A octave, 0.32s) after copying embed code from a card, the batch bar, or the drawer; `delete` (harp A→D, 0.42s) after a confirmed delete, batch delete, or clear-all; `undo` (harp D→A, 0.36s) after a successful undo; `complete` (harp Dadd9 arpeggio into a piano chord with a faint finger cymbal, 1.12s) after a successful import, export, or completed update run; `error` (piano E→D# minor second, 0.42s) whenever an error toast or a failed-save notification appears. Cancelled actions play nothing.
- Defaults: sound effects on (`soundEffects` absent), background music off (`backgroundMusic` absent). Both switches live in the dashboard's 「設定」 popover; the popup and the content script read the same setting. Turning effects on plays `save` as a preview.
- Background music: `sounds/background-music.ogg`, 120 seconds, D major, 64 BPM, 32 bars (piano theme, strings enter, theme an octave higher with harp, closing bars on A7sus4 that resolve into bar 1). The render's tail is folded back onto the start so the `AudioBufferSourceNode` loop has no gap. Dashboard only; never in the popup or on Threads pages.
- Content script access: only `sounds/save.ogg` and `sounds/error.ogg` are web-accessible, and only to the Threads hosts.
- Provenance: composed and rendered with the local XSXB-Band studio from CC0 recordings (upright piano, harp, violin section, cello section, finger cymbals), then encoded to 48kHz Ogg Opus; no music-generation model was used.
- Accessibility: every sound duplicates visible feedback that is also announced through a live region, so muting loses no information.

### 10. Visual Atmosphere
- `body::before` paints four champagne radial glows on a layer 25% larger than the viewport and animates it with `ambientDrift` (28s, alternate: translate, rotate, scale). `body` has `isolation: isolate` so the `z-index: -1` layers sit above the body background and below all content.
- `body::after` is a 560px radial spotlight at `--pointer-x`/`--pointer-y` that fades in while `<html data-pointer="active">`; `.article-card::before` adds a 300px highlight at `--spot-x`/`--spot-y` on hover (cards are `isolation: isolate` so the glow sits under their content). Cards also lift 2px with a warm shadow on hover.
- The top bar is translucent with `backdrop-filter: blur(18px) saturate(1.5)`; the sidebar and list pane are transparent so the glow shows through.
- The dashboard sidebar starts with a welcome card (ink background, champagne hairline and glow, floating mascot) that greets by hour (夜深了 before 05:00, 早安 before 11:00, 午安 before 18:00, otherwise 晚安) and shows the total and the number saved in the last 7 days.
- Reduced motion stops the drift and the mascot float, hides both spotlights, and removes card entrance animations.

## Export & Import Specifications

### Export Formats
All three exports are selection-aware: when posts are checked only those are exported, otherwise the current filtered list is exported.

1. Embed Only: `threads-embed-codes-YYYY-MM-DD.js`
   ```javascript
   const posts = [
       '<blockquote class="text-post-media" data-text-post-permalink="...">...</blockquote>'
   ];
   ```
2. Featured Data: `threads-featured-data-YYYY-MM-DD.js` (Formatted for Threadfolio; author without @ prefix; includes `embeddable` and `embeddableCheckedAt` only for posts that have been checked)
   ```javascript
   const posts = [
       {
           "embedCode": "...",
           "postLink": "https://www.threads.com/@user/post/...",
           "author": "user",
           "content": "...",
           "tags": ["JavaScript"]
       }
   ];
   ```
3. Full Backup Data: `threads-full-data-YYYY-MM-DD.js` (Content, timestamp, tag, and expiry fields, plus `embeddable` and `embeddableCheckedAt` for posts that have been checked. It omits `id`, and import generates a new one.)
   ```javascript
   const posts = [
       {
           "embedCode": "...",
           "postLink": "https://www.threads.com/@user/post/...",
           "author": "user",
           "content": "...",
           "timestamp": "2026-05-29T02:00:00.000Z",
           "timestampTitle": "May 29, 2026, 10:00 AM",
           "savedAt": "2026-05-29T02:10:00.000Z",
           "tags": ["JavaScript"],
           "status": "active",
           "expiredAt": "",
           "expiredReason": "",
           "expiredCheckedAt": ""
       }
   ];
   ```
   Note: `<script>` tags are stripped from `embedCode` on export and re-appended on import.

### Import Pipeline
- Sources: a file picker (`.js` / `.json`) in both surfaces (dashboard sidebar 「匯入」, popup 「更多」 → 「匯入…」), plus a paste-text dialog in the popup. Exports live in the dashboard sidebar 「匯出」 popover, whose label states the scope (「匯出已選取的 N 篇」 or 「匯出目前列表的 N 篇」), and in the popup 「更多」 menu.
- `.json` files are parsed directly with `JSON.parse` (bare array or `{ "savedArticles": [...] }` wrapper). `.js` files and pasted text go through a two-stage parser: `JSON.parse` on the `const posts = [...]` array (the featured and full exports are JSON) -> regular expression extraction of single-quoted embed codes that contain `data-text-post-permalink` (the embed-only export). No `eval`/`new Function` fallback exists, because the extension page CSP blocks dynamic evaluation.
- Modes: Merge (deduplicates on the storage key, i.e. the post code, including duplicates inside the imported file, and inserts new posts by `savedAt`) or Overwrite (replaces the entire database, gated behind a second confirmation modal).

## Security & Content Security Policy (CSP)
- Permissions: `storage`, `unlimitedStorage`, `tabs`, `scripting`
- Web-accessible resources: only `sounds/save.ogg` and `sounds/error.ogg`, matched to the four Threads hosts.
- Minimum Chrome version: 123 (`light-dark()`).
- Host Permissions: `https://www.threads.com/*`, `https://threads.com/*`, `https://www.threads.net/*`, `https://threads.net/*`
- CSP Headers: `script-src 'self'; object-src 'self'; frame-src https://www.threads.com https://www.threads.net https://*.threads.com https://*.threads.net;` (No inline scripts, no remote CDN scripts; the only remote resource is the Google Fonts stylesheet imported by ui.css)
- PostMessage Security: Strict origin allowlist (`threads.net`, `threads.com`, `instagram.com`) plus a bounded height range on incoming iframe resize messages.
- XSS Prevention: Safe text node rendering (`textContent` / `escapeHtml`) for user-controlled strings in dashboard preview metadata, and `sanitizeUrl` for every rendered link or iframe source.
- Storage Safety: `safeStorageGet` / `safeStorageSet` guard against `Extension context invalidated` exceptions after an extension reload.

## Development & Local Testing
- Pure front-end extension with zero build steps and zero local server requirements.
- Clone repository and navigate to `chrome://extensions/` in Chromium-based browsers.
- Enable **Developer Mode** in the top right.
- Click **Load unpacked** and select the project root directory.
- Conventions: no `style` attributes or inline event handlers in HTML (strict CSP; runtime values such as masonry spans, spotlight positions, and stagger indexes are set from JS as CSS variables or single properties), use ui.css tokens and components with only the 12/14/16/20px sizes, register new sounds in `SOUND_EFFECT_FILES` (and in `web_accessible_resources` if Threads pages need them), no native browser dialogs, new modals must implement focus trapping and focus restoration, and any stored-field change must be mirrored in README.md, this file, and the export/import modules.
- Community files (Traditional Chinese): [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) (setup, manual test checklist, commit and PR flow), [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md), [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md) (vulnerabilities go through GitHub private vulnerability reporting, not public issues), [ACCESSIBILITY.md](./ACCESSIBILITY.md) (WCAG 2.2 AA target and known limitations). Issue forms and the PR template live in `.github/`.
